messages:
maya: Heads-up: CI microbench failed on PR #5789 — perf-check flagged a 12% regression on kernel autoselect warmup path. https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/5789
ci-bot: perf-check detected threshold breach for 'kernel_warmup_latency' (baseline=48.2ms, new=54.0ms, delta=12.0%). Run id: perf/2026-03-18-07.
sam: repro runs locally for me on A100: yes seeing the same delta but only for seq_len=1024 workloads. seq_len=256 unaffected.
jordan: interesting — that maps to the autoselect code that switches kernels after warmup. I added extra logging in the PR for kernel decision path.
li: I ran the CI microbench with debug symbols. Dumped kernel selector decisions: first 6 tokens pick fast-kernel-v1, then it flips to slow-kernel-v2 consistently at token 64, which wasn't happening before.
maya: that flip point is the warmup heuristic: if avg_step_latency > 0.8*baseline we bias away. Looks like the baseline estimate is drifting up post-merge. Any PRs that touched baseline computation?
jordan: PR #5762 touched warmup averaging and introduced EWMA alpha change (0.2 -> 0.35). I suspected it was harmless for steady-state but maybe it makes short sequences noisy.
claire: can we bisect between HEAD and v0.23.1 to confirm? I'll fire off a bisect job on the perf harness.
ci-bot: bisect job queued: perf-bisect/5789-run1 (comparing v0.23.1..HEAD). Estimated runtime ~ 45m.
(30m later)
ci-bot: bisect found candidate commit: 0fa9c3a (PR #5762) — reproduces kernel flip and latency delta on seq_len=1024 microbench.
sam: confirmed. Rolling local bisect shows metrics change right at commit 0fa9c3a. Patch looks small but changes EWMA alpha.
li: quick thought: higher alpha weights recent noisy samples more, so the baseline estimate overshoots during variable batches, triggering kernel downgrade prematurely.
maya: OK. Options: revert #5762, tweak alpha back, or change the autoselect threshold margin. Revert would be fastest to get CI green and unblock release.
jordan: agree revert then follow-up PR to add a unit test for warmup stability across short sequences and noisy latencies. Also add a regression test in perf CI targeting seq_len=1024.
claire: I'll open an emergency revert PR and tag release team. @release-bot can you hold the canary?
release-bot: Canary hold requested for release v0.24.0 — ON HOLD by eng-runtime due to perf regression.
maya: I'm pushing the revert PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/5792 (revert of PR #5762). Requesting expedited CI.
ci-bot: PR #5792 triggered perf-check: pending.
(10m later)
ci-bot: perf-check for PR #5792 passed. 'kernel_warmup_latency' restored to baseline (48.1ms).
sam: great. I'll keep monitoring staging canary once we unhold.
li: for follow-ups: propose adding a small synthetic test that injects jitter into step latencies and asserts EWMA baseline doesn't exceed X% within first N tokens. Also add more granular tracing in kernel selector (reason codes for flips).
jordan: I'll draft the test and a safer alpha transition (maybe adapt alpha based on observed variance).
maya: thanks all. Action items: revert landed (#5792), canary held, follow-up test + safer alpha. Keeping thread open for any weirdness during canary ramp. :white_check_mark:
claire: FYI reminded ops: please watch /metrics/kernel_selector/flip_count on staging for next 24h.
(archive note)
ci-bot: thread archived after 24h of inactivity.
